items.title: Deleting + creating the only character of the very first type in a variant type triggers unhandled exception.
items.body:
In the example below where the cursor is immediately after the `V`, pressing backspace emits the exception `Async_kernel: Unhandled exception (Failure "Skel.push_output: split_kids: index out of bounds")`
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ac37171-0da3-45fb-b38e-4b6eda1225da)

This error does not occur for any other items (e.g. deleting the the `SSaa` using only `Backspace`). The issue doesn't happen if the first `+` is not present. The issue also doesn't happen if there are no other type variants specified (e.g.  if it's just `type Exp = + V`.

Similarly, trying to to type the `+` in the below screenshot emit the same exception
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3b689dcd-9b8f-4746-9412-bb614921a854)

Another related error is having a hole like so, `type T = + [] `, and trying to type `+` in the hole (`type T = + +`).

items.title: Certain strings fail to paste invisibly
items.body:
The simplest example is `([)(`; it will print a messages to the console "WARN: zipper_of_string: Invalid_argument("option is None")" but there is no other feedback. This is a minified version of the following, which arose naturalistically during LLM completion experiments:


```
fun (playList, action) ->
  case action
    | PlaySong(id) =>
      let (songs, _) = playList in (songs, Playing(id))
    | PauseCurrentSong =>
      let (songs, state) = playList in
      case state
        | Playing(id) => (songs, PausedOn(id))
        | _ => playList
      end
    | RemoveSong(id) =>
      let (songs, state) = playList in
      (List.remove(id, songs),
       case state
         | Playing(id') if id == id' => NoSongSelected
         | PausedOn(id') if id == id' => NoSongSelected
         | _ => state
       end)
    | AddSong(id) =>
      let (songs, state) = playList in (List.append(songs, [id]), state)
  end
```

(the problematic part is the 'if' that the llm is trying to use as a 'when' clause).

Likely a wontfix, pending the new syntax model, but I'm logging it.

items.title: Minus parsing issue
items.body: Currently `1-2` will be parsed as `1><-2`. This occurs because `-` has three interpretations; as an Int infix op, an Int prefix op, and as a possible leading character of Int and Float literals. The remolding logic takes care of switching between the first two molds as-appropriate, but remolding can't affect the latter as remolding does not retokenize. Currently when typing `2` on `1-|`, the logic asks if `2` can be appended to the previous token `-`, resulting in a valid token; it can, so it does so, even though this necessitates inserting grout. Not obvious to me what the principled approach is here.
